findings.title: Dead-code `===` comparison for zero-length date overrides never evaluates true
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two separately-created Dayjs object instances with reference equality. Two different `dayjs()` calls never return the same object reference, so this condition is always `false`, even when the override truly has start === end (the common representation of a date override that blocks an entire day). Because this branch is unreachable, a date override meant to mark a whole day unavailable for a fixed host/organizer will not be detected here, and the slot can still be considered available — directly undermining the goal of this PR (respecting fixed-host date overrides).

findings.title: Working-hours check never flags a day the host has no entries for at all
findings.body: The `workingHours.find((workingHour) => { if (workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day())) {...} })` guard at lines 139-148 only evaluates the out-of-range condition for workingHours entries whose `days` already include the slot's weekday. If a fixed host has no workingHours entry at all for that weekday (i.e. a day off with zero availability rows), none of the entries ever return `true`, `.find()` returns `undefined`, and the surrounding `if` is skipped entirely — the function falls through to the busy-time check instead of returning `false`. As a result, a fixed host who simply does not work on a given day is still treated as available for that day as long as there is no conflicting busy time. This is exactly the scenario this PR claims to fix for round-robin events (slots should not be offered when the fixed host is unavailable), so this logic gap leaves the core bug only partially fixed.

findings.title: `end` variable duplicates `start`, so slot end time is never checked against working-hours close time
findings.body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is computed identically to the `start` variable on the preceding line, instead of being derived from the slot's end time (e.g. using `slotEndTime`/`eventLength`). Consequently `end > workingHour.endTime` is equivalent to re-checking `start > workingHour.endTime`, so a slot that starts within business hours but whose duration would push it past the host's configured closing time is never flagged as out of bounds. This can let round-robin/collective bookings be offered that run past a fixed host's working hours.

findings.title: `dateOverrides.find()` short-circuits on the first same-day override, breaking multi-range overrides
findings.body: The availability decision for date overrides (lines 106-131) is based on the first override entry whose date matches the slot's date, via `Array.prototype.find`. If a user has more than one override time range configured for the same calendar date (e.g. a split day with a morning and an afternoon range), and the slot falls within the second range but not the first, the first entry's callback already sets `dateOverrideExist = true` and returns `true` (since `slotStartTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end)...)` for the earlier range), causing `.find()` to stop and the outer `if` to return `false` (unavailable) for a slot that is actually covered by the later range. This produces incorrect 'unavailable' results whenever a date has multiple override ranges.

findings.title: No automated test for the headline round-robin fixed-host date-override fix
findings.body: The PR description states its primary goal is to ensure round-robin events respect a fixed host's date overrides so slots aren't offered when the fixed host is unavailable. The only tests added ('Check for Date overrides' and its new timezone variant) use a single-user event type with `hosts: []` and no `schedulingType`, so they never exercise the `fixedHosts`/`isFixed` branch together with a `ROUND_ROBIN` schedulingType and a date override. There is no regression test creating a round-robin event with a fixed host that has a date override, verifying that slots outside that override are excluded while the round-robin (non-fixed) host's own availability does not override it — the exact scenario this PR claims to fix.

findings.title: `timeZone` added as optional but is now functionally required for correct override math
findings.body: `TimeRange.timeZone` was added as an optional field, yet `packages/lib/slots.ts` now relies on it (`dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)`) to compute the organizer's UTC offset for a date override. Nothing in the type enforces that every caller supplies it; if a `DateOverride`/`TimeRange` is constructed without `timeZone` (e.g. by another call site not updated in this PR), `dayjs(...).tz(undefined)` silently falls back to the dayjs-timezone plugin's 'guess' (the server process's local timezone) instead of erroring, which would silently produce incorrect slot times rather than surfacing the missing data.
